title: Excretory and Reproductive Systems
seo_title: Grade 6 Science: Excretory and Reproductive Systems Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Multicellular organisms rely on internal systems: the basic structures and functions of the excretory system (kidneys, bladder, lungs, skin) and the reproductive system, and how body systems work together. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 6, Biology)
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 science worksheets (BC): the kidneys and bladder, removing wastes, the male and female reproductive systems, puberty and development. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The excretory system removes wastes from the body.
key_sub: The kidneys filter the blood to make urine.
body_html:
How to think about it

Cells make wastes. The kidneys filter the blood and make urine, which is stored in the bladder. The lungs remove carbon dioxide, and the skin removes some water and salt in sweat.

The reproductive system makes sex cells. Sperm are made in the testes and eggs in the ovaries. When a sperm joins an egg (fertilization), a baby can develop in the uterus, getting food and oxygen through the placenta. Puberty is when the body becomes able to reproduce.

Example

Which organ filters the blood to make urine?

There are two of them, in your lower back.

Answer: the kidneys

Example

Where does a baby develop?

A muscular organ in the female body

Answer: the uterus

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the stomach makes urine.
  • Thinking only the kidneys remove wastes (the lungs and skin do too).
  • Mixing up the ovary and the uterus.
